schema.description: Proof-specification identifier used to select the behavioral UI contract.

strict.description: When true, missing evidence, unknown solver results, and undeclared behavior fail validation.

description.description: Human-readable purpose of this proof specification; it does not replace executable invariants.

name.description: Stable application name used in reports, evidence namespaces, and recipes.

build_source.description: Command, artifact reference, or source location used to build the application under test.

default_base_url.description: Default absolute URL used when a screen or oracle does not specify a base URL.

engine.description: Browser engine used for automation; consumers must pin the corresponding browser build.

locale.description: BCP-47 locale injected into the browser context for deterministic formatting.

timezone.description: IANA timezone injected into the browser context.

color_scheme.description: Browser color-scheme preference used to exercise theme-sensitive rendering.

name.description: Required SMT solver; the proof semantics are defined for Z3.

version.description: Pinned Z3 version used to reproduce the result.

determinism_mechanism.description: Deterministic Z3 resource accounting mechanism; wall-clock timeouts are not substitutes.

id.description: Stable screen ID shared with the screen register.

route.description: Exact route path the browser must open; route parameters must be represented by a fixture.

source.description: Source or generated artifact reference used to trace this proof back to implementation.

selector.description: Stable semantic selector proving that the expected screen root is present.

initial_state.description: Named finite-state-machine state required immediately after navigation and fixture setup.

items.description: Allowed named state in the screen model.

fixture.description: Deterministic fixture identifier used to seed the screen's data and identity context.

items.description: Identity roles permitted to execute this screen proof.
Evidence kinds required from the browser run, such as `dom`, `accessibility`, `network`, or `audit`.

id.description: Stable control identifier referenced by transitions and assertions.

kind.description: Control semantic type, such as `button`, `input`, `link`, `select`, or `table`.

selector.description: Stable semantic selector used to locate and interact with this control.

items.description: Roles allowed to see or operate this control.

id.description: Stable transition identifier referenced by journeys, traces, and failure reports.

action.description: Control action or semantic event that triggers the transition.

from.description: Named source state from which this transition is valid.

to.description: Named destination state required after the action completes.

items.description: Roles authorized to perform this transition.
Preconditions that must hold before the action is attempted.
Postconditions that must hold after the action completes.
API operation or route expected to be invoked by the transition.
Audit event identifiers or predicates expected after the transition.
Notification or outbox event identifiers expected after the transition.

id.description: Stable assertion identifier used in evidence and reports.

after.description: Transition ID or named event after which this assertion is evaluated.

kind.description: Assertion semantics selecting the verifier to run.

api.description: API field, route, or response expression compared with the UI.

ui_selector.description: Selector identifying the UI value or region under assertion.

comparison.description: Explicit comparison operator or mapping rule, such as `equals`, `contains`, or `matches`.

condition.description: Predicate that must be true for the assertion to pass.

expected.description: Expected scalar value for the assertion; the verifier compares it using the declared comparison rule.

id.description: Stable invariant identifier included in solver results and recipes.

description.description: Plain-language statement of the safety or correctness property being proved.

items.description: Screen, state, role, or fixture names to which the invariant applies.

formula.description: Finite-domain logical formula encoded for Z3; it must describe the negation of the desired property.

counterexample.description: Named artifact or projection describing the counterexample returned when the formula is satisfiable.

id.description: Stable end-to-end journey identifier used in browser traces.

name.description: Human-readable journey name shown in reports.

role.description: Role or identity under which every journey step executes.

fixture.description: Fixture namespace or record set used to make the journey reproducible.

expected_final_state.description: Named state that must hold when the journey finishes.

items.description: Evidence kinds that must be present for the journey to pass.

screen.description: Screen ID from the proof specification at this journey step.

transition.description: Transition ID executed on the referenced screen.

mode.description: Oracle mode; `independent` requires a read path separate from the UI automation path.

base_url.description: Absolute base URL used by the independent oracle.

database_read_model.description: Read-only database/model projection used to compare committed application state.

audit_log.description: Audit-log or audit-chain projection used to verify recorded actions.
